newsitem.title: UK: Cadbury-Schweppes H1 profits to fall flat.
newsitem.headline: Cadbury-Schweppes H1 profits to fall flat.

text.p: Cadbury-Schweppes Plc is expected to report flat half-year profits on Wednesday, held back by the impact of sterling's strength on foreign exchange markets and the loss of earnings from Coca-Cola Schweppes Beverages Ltd (CCSB), said analysts.
Cadbury-Schweppes sold its 51 percent stake in Britain's CCSB to Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc in June for 623 million stg.

Analysts forecast pre-tax profits in the six months to June 30, 1997 will range from 227 to 246 million stg, little changed from 231 million for the same period last year. Dividend forecasts are centred on 5.5 pence per share.

Brokers estimates include an expected 20 million stg hit from the impact of sterling strength against overseas currencies in the period but excludes profits from the sale of the group's interest in CCSB.
"We will be very much focused on volume sales in the United States, the real question for Cadbury Schweppes remains: can it compete successfully with Coke and Pepsi?", said one analyst.

Analysts estimate the group will generate about 122 million stg of earnings from its U.S. drinks business while trading profits from its confectionery side will stay flat at some 105 million. The confectionery business tends to perform better in the second half as sales pick-up in colder weather and the Christmas period.

In May chairman Dominic Cadbury told shareholders the group would show further progress in 1997, despite seeing some adverse impact from the strength of sterling. Cadbury-Schweppes earns less than 10 percent of its profits in Britain.

He also said the group's beverage operations were performing well so far in 1997 but its confectionery markets had experienced a slow start to the year, although market share was "holding up well or increasing".
In April, the group announced weak soft drinks sales figures for the U.S. in the first quarter, showing volume sales of soft drinks in the U.S. up one percent.
Soft drinks sales in the Americas account for around 60 percent of the group's beverage sales world-wide and the region makes up just under 30 percent of total group beverage and confectionery sales.
Cadbury is third in the U.S. soft drinks market to Coca-Cola and PepsiCo Inc.

Cadbury-Schweppes shares have shown marked volatility in recent months amid rumours of a take-over bid by Unilever Plc and heavy buying by U.S. investors. Some U.S. fund managers view Cadbury-Schweppes as on a low rating relative to its international peer group like Coke and Pepsico.
Cadbury-Schweppes shares were 1-1/2 pence lower at 588p at 1345 GMT.
